courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Beginning Ballet
courses.description: The technique and vocabulary of classical ballet are presented. Exercises at the barre are followed by practice and combinations in the center. Previously offered as PHYA 208.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Introduction to Dance Technique
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the positions, exercises, and steps common to ballet, jazz, and modern dance. It is designed for students with no previous dance experience and is a prerequisite for EXSS 10 , 12 , and 13 . Previously offered as PHYA 212.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Beginning Modern Dance
courses.description: Students will explore the principles of movement that define modern dance, gaining some understanding of the use of weight, the shape of the body in space, an awareness of timing and energy, and individual creative potential. Previously offered as PHYA 224.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Beginning Jazz Dance
courses.description: Students will explore the roots of the jazz style through rhythm, principles of isolation and opposition, shape and energy through center work, stretches, movement across the floor, and simple routines. Previous ballet training is highly recommended. Previously offered as PHYA 220.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Intermediate Ballet
courses.description: For the dancer with a solid understanding of the basics of ballet and several years' dance training. It emphasizes more sophisticated steps in longer combinations. Previously offered as PHYA 308.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Intermediate Jazz Dance
courses.description: Students will explore the jazz style in greater complexity plus gain understanding of jazz music as it relates to jazz dance. It includes center work, complex movement phrases across floor, adagio, and routines using large movement vocabulary. At least two years of dance and familiarity with jazz style are recommended. Previously offered as PHYA 320.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Intermediate Modern Dance
courses.description: Students will work to develop greater technical skill and continue a more advanced exploration of modern dance principles of effort-shape through center work and phrases of greater length and complexity in the center and across the floor. At least two years of modern dance training are recommended. Previously offered as PHYA 324.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Advanced Ballet
courses.description: For the dancer with substantial background in ballet. Speed, endurance, multiple turns, beats, and complicated combinations are emphasized. Previously offered as PHYA 408.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Heart of the Play: Fundamentals of Acting, Playwriting, and Collaboration
courses.description: This seminar is designed to get the student doing theatre, sparking creativity, and making connections with the deeper lessons of this dynamic art form. Students will write, stage, and perform their own 10-minute plays.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Psychology of Clothes: Motivations for Dressing Up and Dressing Down
courses.description: The course seeks to help students find ways to articulate their own motivations for dress and then apply the ideas they have discovered to the ways in which individuality as well as group attitudes are expressed through clothing. Honors version available.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Staging America: The American Drama
courses.description: This seminar examines American drama from its colonial origins to the present as both a literary and commercial art form. The focus throughout will be on the forces that shaped American drama as well as drama's ability to shed light on the national experience. Honors version available.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Spectacle in the Theatre
courses.description: This course examines how the theatrical designer uses scenery, costumes, and lighting to help create a production. Students will apply these techniques in creating their own design projects.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Documentary Theatre
courses.description: This course explores the political and social ramifications of documentary theatre in the United States. Students will investigate a local community of their choosing and create an interview-based performance. Honors version available.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Style: A Mode of Expression
courses.description: This seminar studies the elements of design in their pure form, surveys a history of period styles and theatre, and identifies their causes. Honors version available.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: First Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: This is a special topics course. Content will vary.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Perspectives in Drama
courses.description: A survey of plays from the Greeks to the present, analyzed through such elements of the dramatic text as action, character, structure, and language. Honors version available.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Perspectives in the Theatre: Page to Stage
courses.description: A survey of the interrelationships of acting, directing, designing, and playwriting through the study of major periods of theatrical expression and representative plays. Honors version available.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Perspectives in World Drama
courses.description: A survey of non-Western drama and theatre with emphasis on the historical and aesthetic development of those regions. Honors version available.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Play Analysis
courses.description: Development of the skill to analyze plays for academic and production purposes through the intensive study of representative plays. DRAM 120 is the first course in the major and the minor in dramatic art. Honors version available.

source.text: DRAM 120. | 3 Credits. | FY-LAUNCH (only designated sections), FC-AESTH.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Acting for Nonmajors
courses.description: Introduction to basic processes and techniques of acting for the stage.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Voice Training I
courses.description: Fundamental principles underlying the effective use of voice and speech in performance.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Acting the Song
courses.description: The course explores how to gain facility in expression and truthfulness in action while communicating through a dramatic song. Challenges include how to navigate a scene that moves into song and how to manage breath and vulnerability in performance. Permission of the instructor required.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Beginning Acting for the Major
courses.description: Introduction to acting tools, emphasizing playing actions and pursuing an objective by personalized given circumstances. Performance work drawn from short scripted, improvised, and contemporary scenes.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Introduction to the American Stage Musical
courses.description: A topical survey of musical theater repertoire from its early inception in 18th-century Europe to current 21st-century incarnations. Various stylistic approaches, historical periods, and creative contributions to the genre will be explored. Examination of case studies through diverse perspectives of class, gender and race will situate the repertoire in a broad artistic and social context.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Performers' Awareness
courses.description: This course focuses on developing body and mind awareness and undoing habits (including habits of thought) which restrict the performer. The class explores strategies for reducing tension, re-discovering natural alignment, and replacing self-judgement with self-confidence.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Movement for the Actor
courses.description: Introduction to physical training. Individual/group exercises explore relaxation, breath, concentration, flexibility, and imaginative response that become physical tools for acting. May include stage combat, juggling, mime, improvisation, games, and yoga.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Physical Comedy, Farce Techniques, and Clown
courses.description: Beginning with a history of physical comedy and performance techniques, this experiential class will explore vulnerability and self-discovery through clown. Students will learn farce techniques which strengthen physical agility and comic timing. Through a process of rediscovering innocence in sound and movement, the student will begin to forget the filter of the socialized body, achieving a heightened presence.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Stagecraft
courses.description: General survey of materials, equipment, and processes used in technical theatre.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: The Playful Actor: Theatre Games and Improvisation
courses.description: This course seeks to strengthen the powers of imagination, courage, spontaneity, and presence of the actor through theatre games and improvisation.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Technical Methods: Scenery
courses.description: DRAM 191 or 192 required for dramatic art majors. Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Introduction to equipment, procedures, and personnel in the design and execution of plans for scenery, lighting, properties, and sound for theatrical productions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Technical Methods: Costume
courses.description: DRAM 191 or 192 required for dramatic art majors. Introduction to equipment, procedures, and personnel in the design and execution of costumes for theatrical productions. Permission of the instructor for nonmajors.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Production Practicum
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Required for the dramatic art major. Practicum in production with PlayMakers Repertory Company in costuming, scenery, lighting, sound, or theatre management.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Dramatic Art Projects
courses.description: Permission of the department. May be repeated for credit. Restricted to juniors and seniors majoring in dramatic art. Intensive individual work in major areas of theatrical production: design, technical, directing, acting, playwriting, management.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Musical Theatre Workshop
courses.description: This course will serve an initial music rehearsals for the spring production. Students will learn their role's songs, focusing on proper vocal technique and accurate notes and rhythms. By audition and permission of instructor.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Theatre Histories
courses.description: This course introduces students to theatre histories and cultures from India, Asia, Africa, and Latin America, with reference to Western European/North American traditions. Students will investigate how drama, theatre, and performance develops both within individual cultural milieus and through contact with other cultures.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Theatre of the Word
courses.description: This course, with a theatre and social justice theme, is structured to give students an understanding of the role of the speaker before the public, the logical and sequential development of an idea, and the methodology for organizing and presenting materials and information. The course will cover information gathering, speech outlining, small group discussion, and provide extemporaneous, informative, and persuasive speaking opportunities.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Playwriting I
courses.description: Permission of the department. A practical course in writing for the stage with studio productions of selected works.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Voice Training II
courses.description: A continuation of DRAM 140 .

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Acting for the Camera
courses.description: The process of acting and its relationship to the technical and artistic demands of television/film production. Problems of continuity and out-of-sequence filming. Concentration and thinking on camera.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, DRAM 135 or 150; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: DRAM 245. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, DRAM 135 or 150 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Intermediate Acting for the Major
courses.description: A deeper exploration of fulfilled actions prompted by an objective, with emphasis on developing techniques required by more formally structured texts such as Sophocles, Molière, Ibsen, Shaw, and Chekhov.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Movement for the Actor II
courses.description: Development of balance, flexibility, strength, focus, grace, and precision through martial art of T'ai Chi Ch'uan. Emphasis on applying T'ai Chi principles to acting. Chinese philosophical bases for T'ai Chi explored.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, DRAM 155; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: DRAM 255. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, DRAM 155 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Advanced Stagecraft
courses.description: The course provides practical applications of principles and techniques used in technical theatre. Lectures are supported by individually scheduled workshop sessions where techniques are applied to a theatrical production.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, DRAM 160; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

source.text: DRAM 260. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, DRAM 160 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-CREATE, HI-PERFORM.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Introduction to Theatrical Design
courses.description: General principles of scenic, costume, and lighting design for the theatre.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Introduction to Theatre Management
courses.description: An overview of the major functions of management in the American nonprofit theatre including marketing, fundraising, finances, strategy and operations. Presentation skills will be practiced.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Theatre History and Literature I
courses.description: Survey of theatre practice and writing from the Greeks to 1700.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Theatre History and Literature II
courses.description: Survey of theatre practice and writing from 1700 to 1920.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Theatre History and Literature III
courses.description: Survey of theatre practice and writing from 1930 to the present.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Studies in Dramatic Theory and Criticism
courses.description: May be repeated for credit. Seminar in dramatic theory and criticism with emphasis on the modern period. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Modern British Drama
courses.description: Evolution of modern British drama from 1956 through the present. Honors version available.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: African American Theatre
courses.description: This course investigates the history and legacy of African American drama through the study of its literary texts, performance styles, and cultural history.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Theatre for Social Change
courses.description: This course assesses different models of theatre for social change through change theory, playwriting, and collaboration. Students will be guided through the process of creating new works.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Special Topics in Dramatic Art
courses.description: The study of a topic in dramaturgy, theatrical design, or theatrical production. Content and instructor will vary. May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: "Corner of the Sky": The American Musical
courses.description: This course considers the anatomy and diversity of the American musical, exploring its history and aesthetics and employing an interdisciplinary approach to examining and celebrating its shows, sounds, stars, structures, styles, and sensibilities, within the genre's dominant contexts of Broadway, Hollywood, and Utopia.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Arts Criticism
courses.description: An introduction to the principles of arts criticism through study of the work of a variety of critics, by distinguishing between the nature of criticism and reviewing the arts (both performing and plastic), and through the students' own practice of critical writing by means of a series of short essays.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Special Topics in Dramatic Art, FC-CREATE
courses.description: The study of a topic in dramaturgy, theatrical design, or theatrical production. Content and instructor will vary.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Directing
courses.description: Generally limited to majors. An introductory course in the principles of stage directing; analysis for concept, organization of production, and methodology of staging.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, DRAM 120; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: DRAM 300. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, DRAM 120 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Playwriting II
courses.description: A practical course in writing for the theatre, taught at an advanced level.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, DRAM 231; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: DRAM 331. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, DRAM 231 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Theatrical Auditions
courses.description: Practice in the techniques necessary for successful auditions for the theatre. Previously offered as DRAM 134. Permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Musical Scene Study
courses.description: This course builds on the skills acquired in Acting the Song and applies them in the context of a full scene. The course addresses how and why songs occur in the text of musicals, how to transition from dialogue to song and back again, and how to incorporate underscoring in scene work. It incorporates material from different styles and genres: the ''Golden Age'' (Oklahoma, Guys and Dolls, Gypsy) through the 60's/70's (Sweet Charity, Baby, Company) to the present (Rent, Wicked, Parade).

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Advanced Acting for the Major
courses.description: Development of the actor's technique in verse drama with emphasis on scansion and textual analysis as guidelines for actions, characterization, and given circumstances. Scene and monologue work drawn from the works of Shakespeare.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, DRAM 250; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: DRAM 350. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, DRAM 250 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-AESTH.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Original Theatre Works: Methods, Aesthetics, and Creation
courses.description: This course harnesses the creative imagination of those wanting to create their own original performances. Using the tools of devised theatre, an ensemble-based, collaborative approach to creating original works, the course focuses on ensemble collaboration, expanding aesthetic vocabularies, devising new creation methods, and developing unique voices.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Introduction to Projection Design and Mapping
courses.description: This course aims to provide an in-depth understanding of projection mapping in the context of theatre and entertainment design. Through a combination of theoretical and hands-on learning, students will gain the skills necessary to conceptualize, design, and implement projection mapping projects.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Exploring Costumes in Film
courses.description: This course introduces the costume design theory and processes used by professional designers.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Theatre, Law, and American Values
courses.description: Exploration of the way citizens have impacted and transformed American society through their active participation in local, state, and federal governments. Students will examine plays written about or inspired by legal cases and political arguments. Students will research journals, government reports, interviews and correspondence to learn how theatre artists engage in writing about laws and government actions, and will write their own plays based on court cases and current events.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Professional Theatre Laboratory
courses.description: Permission of the department. Individual programs or internship in acting, directing, design, management, and playwriting under the guidance of professional practitioners in conjunction with PlayMakers Repertory Company or other professional theatre organizations.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Special Topics in Dramatic Art, FC-AESTH
courses.description: The study of a topic in dramaturgy, theatrical design, or theatrical production. Content and instructor will vary.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Advanced Directing
courses.description: Advanced Directing (Directing II) will delve further into the role of director and what is needed to achieve successful storytelling for the stage. With an emphasis on text analysis and communication, the classroom becomes a laboratory where students have the opportunity to direct multiple scenes, devised work, and enhance their vocabulary for discussing the work. They will also explore the current world of professional directors and their approaches to the work. By the end of this course, students will know the importance of having a point of view and what it means to be a leader within the creative process.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Playwriting Workshop
courses.description: As image makers, the work we do has a powerful and lasting impact on perception. When writing beyond ourselves and our experience, special care must be given the development of characters and exploration of the world of the play. This class explores the impact of social identity on playwriting and how we can use the power of storytelling to reflect a greater vision for humanity.

source.text: DRAM 431. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, DRAM 231 and DRAM 331 .

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Stage Management
courses.description: Permission of the department. A study of the basic principles and practices of modern stage management.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Sound Design
courses.description: The study of general principles of sound design for the theatre. Theory and application of sound design techniques for the stage, including script analysis, staging concepts, special effects, sound plots, and technology.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Scene Design
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. General principles of visual design as applied to scenery for the theatre. Instruction in standard techniques of planning and rendering scene design.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Costume Design I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Studies and practicum in play analysis and costume design for the theatre. Instruction in techniques of planning and rendering costume design.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Lighting Design I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. General principles of lighting design as applied to the performing arts. Theory and instruction in standard techniques of lighting for the stage.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Survey of Costume History
courses.description: A survey of historic costume forms from ancient Egypt to the present time. Honors version available.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Studies in Dramaturgy and Criticism
courses.description: This seminar seeks to introduce students to the principles of arts criticism through study of the work of a variety of different critics, by distinguishing between the nature of criticism and reviewing the arts, and through the students' own practice of critical writing.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Latin American Theatre
courses.description: This course explores the historical and aesthetic development of Latin American theatre, focusing on particular factors that distinguish this theatre from the Western European tradition.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: United States Latino/a Theatre
courses.description: Investigation of United States Latino/a theatre texts and performance practices as a discreet genre. United States Latino/a theatre will be distinguished from the dominant culture, and the diversity of forms and styles will be discussed.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Issues in Arts Management
courses.description: Arts management issues taught through analysis of case studies. Course includes management theories, organizational structures, and current issues.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Theatre Management
courses.description: Practicum in theatre management procedures and business of the theatre involving box office, audience development, research, publicity, operational, and contract procedures in regard to artists, technicians, managers, and producers. Students actively engage in management areas of the PlayMakers Repertory Company and productions of the Department of Dramatic Art.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Costume Seminars I: Dyeing and Painting
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Taught in a four-semester rotation. May be repeated for credit for a total of six hours for undergraduates and 12 hours for graduate students. Series of topics in costume for use in design and production for the stage.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Advanced Special Topics in Dramatic Art
courses.description: The study of a topic in dramaturgy, theatrical design, or theatrical production for advanced undergraduates and graduate students. Content and instructor will vary. May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Media in Performance
courses.description: Required preparation, one performance studies course above COMM 400. Permission of the instructor for students lacking the required preparation. Project-based class where students acquire skills and critical approaches to create collaborative, professional, multimedia works.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Costume Design for the Body
courses.description: Study of proportions and the effects of corsetry and body padding to body proportions. This class requires permission of the instructor.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, DRAM 192 or permission of the instructor.

source.text: DRAM 667. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, DRAM 192 or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Honors Project in Dramatic Art
courses.description: Required preparation, 3.3 cumulative grade point average and permission of the department. The commencement of a special project (essay or creative endeavor), approved by the department, by a student who has been designated a candidate for undergraduate honors.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Honors Project in Dramatic Art
courses.description: Permission of the department. The completion of a special project by a student who has been designated a candidate for undergraduate honors.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: Close study of the interrelationships between theory and practice in contemporary world theatre, placing developments in their cultural contexts, and exploring current theatrical trends in an international framework.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Acting I
courses.description: Admission to the M.F.A. Acting program required. Intensive professional training for the actor. Must be taken fall and spring.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Acting II
courses.description: Admission to the second year of the M.F.A. Acting program required. Advanced professional training for the actor. Must be taken fall and spring.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Voice I
courses.description: Admission to the M.F.A. Acting program required. Development of the individual actor's voice and speech. Must be taken fall and spring.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Voice II
courses.description: Admission to the second year of the M.F.A. Acting program required. Expansion of the individual's vocal versatility in performance. Must be taken fall and spring.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Movement I
courses.description: Admission to the M.F.A. Acting program required. Development of the actor's body as an expressive instrument. Must be taken fall and spring.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Movement II
courses.description: Acting program required. Advanced projects in movement. Special sessions in Physical Comedy and Clown. Must be taken fall and spring. Admission to the second year of the M.F.A.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Rehearsal and Performance I
courses.description: Admission to the M.F.A. Acting program required. Rehearsal and performance of special ensemble projects. Must be taken fall and spring. May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Rehearsal and Performance II
courses.description: Admission to the second year of the M.F.A. Acting program required. Practical application of techniques in rehearsal and performance in studio and main stage production. Must be taken fall and spring. May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Acting Practicum I
courses.description: Admission to the third year of the M.F.A. Acting program required. Intense practicum as a member of the PlayMakers Repertory acting company. Preparation and presentation of assigned projects and work in departmental productions. Work in voice and movement as scheduled.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Costume Seminars II: Millinery
courses.description: Advanced costume production techniques with an emphasis on millinery. Undergraduates-Instructor permission only. Permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Costume Seminars III: Masks and Armor
courses.description: Advanced costume production techniques with an emphasis on creating masks and armor.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Costume Seminars IV: Decorative Arts
courses.description: Advanced costume production techniques with an emphasis on decorative arts, with an emphasis on fans and shoes. This class requires permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Costume Production I: Couture Methods
courses.description: Advanced construction techniques in theatrical costuming with an emphasis on couture methods. This class requires permission of the instructor.

source.text: DRAM 740. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, DRAM 192 for undergraduates.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Advanced Special Studies: Costume Production II: Advanced Couture Methods
courses.description: Advanced construction techniques with an emphasis on advanced couture methods. Graduate students only.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Special Studies: Costume Production III: Tailoring
courses.description: Costume graduates only. Advanced construction techniques with an emphasis on bodice development. Costume graduate students only.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Costume Construction III: Advanced Pattern Making
courses.description: Study of pattern making in advanced shapes for the stage. Graduate students only.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Costume Construction IV: Advanced Pattern Making
courses.description: Continued study of pattern making with advanced shapes for theatrical costumes. Graduate students only.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Costume Construction V: Creative Draping
courses.description: Using combination of patternmaking and dressmaking techniques to achieve unusual shapes in theatrical costume. Graduate students only.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Digital Technology in Costume Production
courses.description: Permission of instructor. Investigation of digital applications as applies to professional development for costume makers.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: World Costume
courses.description: Explores a variety of techniques and understanding of traditional garments as it pertains to non-Western cultures. The goal of the class is learning from outside experts utilizing their perspective and knowledge to bring an in-depth examination of clothing from around the world.

courses.subject: DRAM
courses.title: Period Pattern I: Pre-Victorian
courses.description: Advanced study of western fashion from the 14th through 18th Centuries. Graduate students only.

courses.subject: DRAM
